documents.unit: Center for Teaching Excellence and Innovation
documents.title: Your Classroom Faculty Guide to AI
documents.stance_why: The guide sets no binding rule; it advises faculty to "set clear expectations" about "whether and how" students may use AI, to allow it "only for certain purposes" if they choose, and to "require specific disclosures or citations". The decision is handed to instructors, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: An advisory teaching-center guide for Rush faculty. It defines AI, urges instructors to set their own expectations and require AI use disclosures and citations, and suggests redesigning assessments to reduce AI vulnerability. It warns against relying on AI detectors and encourages faculty to lean into AI. No computing-specific content.

units.why: The guide defines AI in general; this is a definition that sets what the guide covers ("the creation of computer systems that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence"), so it is P61 with informs modality.
units.anchor: the creation of computer systems that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence

units.why: Defines generative AI ("a type of artificial intelligence that is designed to create new and original content"), fixing the scope of the guide; P61 definition, informs.
units.anchor: a type of artificial intelligence that is designed to create new and original content

units.why: Names ethical concerns ("privacy, job displacement, and biases in decision-making") as a caveat to AI benefits; this is P53 naming harms, informs.
units.anchor: there are ethical concerns about privacy, job displacement, and biases in decision-making

units.why: Warns of "ethical implications and potential misuse" including generating "false content or manipulate information"; a harms statement (P53) rather than a conduct ban, so informs.
units.anchor: it can also be used to generate false content or manipulate information
units.fit_note: Also flags misuse (false content) but states no conduct rule, so P74 does not fit.

units.why: Advises educators to "start with a clear pedagogical purpose" for AI in the classroom; instructors are the actor, it is advice (should) on designing AI use before the course, closest to P35 course redesign around AI.
units.anchor: it is crucial to start with a clear pedagogical purpose
units.fit_note: Advice to design AI activities with a learning purpose; not a grading or assignment redesign rule as such.

units.why: Says "AI should be seen as a tool to support and enhance teaching and learning, rather than replace human interaction", keeping humans central; nearest type is P32 (AI must not replace thinking/people), though it is about human interaction in teaching.
units.anchor: AI should be seen as a tool to support and enhance teaching and learning
units.frag_start: a learner-centered approach is essential. AI should
units.fit_note: Concerns AI not replacing human interaction in teaching, not students remaining primary problem-solver.

units.why: Recommends designing "AI-enabled activities that encourage student engagement, critical thinking, and creativity" and giving students chances to interact with AI; this welcomes AI use in teaching, so P02 encourage.
units.anchor: design AI-enabled activities that encourage student engagement, critical thinking, and creativity

units.why: States that creating opportunities to interact with AI "fosters digital literacy and prepares them for the AI-driven world"; a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: fosters digital literacy and prepares them for the AI-driven world they will face
units.frag_start: Creating opportunities for students to interact

units.why: Says "ongoing professional development is crucial for educators" with training and support so faculty understand AI; faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty members should be provided with the necessary training and support to understand AI technologies

units.why: Lists "professional learning communities or workshops" as platforms to share practices on AI; faculty community support, P63.
units.anchor: professional learning communities or workshops

units.why: Notes that "using AI sources can be helpful for students to brainstorm, edit, translate, or generate ideas"; it identifies permitted student uses (brainstorming), so P15 with informs modality, and also writing-support uses.
units.anchor: Using AI sources can be helpful for students to brainstorm, edit, translate, or generate ideas
units.frag_start: Using AI sources can be helpful
units.fit_note: Also names editing and translation (prose), which P18 covers; brainstorming chosen as first-listed use.

units.why: Tells instructors to "set clear expectations" on "whether and how" students can use AI, possibly only for certain purposes; a requirement-like instruction to communicate rules per assignment, P09 rather than P04 because the focus is stating expectations.
units.anchor: for your students on whether and how they can use AI sources in your assignments
units.fit_note: Applies to assignments, not specifically the syllabus; also leaves the permit/forbid choice to the instructor (P04).

units.why: Says the instructor "may want to allow it only for certain purposes or require specific disclosures", leaving the choice to each instructor; P04.
units.anchor: You may want to allow it only for certain purposes or require specific disclosures

units.why: Instructs faculty to "discuss with your students how to check the facts" because text AI "may write responses without concern for factual accuracy"; verification of AI output, P31, and a discussion with students.
units.anchor: Discuss with your students how to check the facts!
units.fit_note: Directs instructors to discuss fact-checking with students; also relates to P66.

units.why: States AI tools "sometimes completely make up information or fake source citations"; this is the hallucination fact behind verifying output, P31 informs.
units.anchor: sometimes completely make up information or fake source citations

units.why: Tells instructors to "encourage your students to use non-AI sources to verify accuracy and to cite those non-AI sources" instead of AI content; verification of AI output, P31.
units.anchor: use non-AI sources to verify accuracy and to cite those non-AI sources
units.fit_note: Also says to cite non-AI sources instead of the AI content.

units.why: "Require your students to declare their use of AI sources with an AI Use Disclosure" describing tool and use; a disclosure-with-submission requirement addressed to instructors, P24.
units.anchor: with an AI Use Disclosure
units.fit_note: Phrased as guidance to instructors ("require your students"), not a binding rule; statement must say which tool and how used.

units.why: Asks that students include the disclosure "even if they only used AI tools for brainstorming or other preparation"; scope of disclosure covers minor uses, P24.
units.anchor: even if they only used AI tools for brainstorming or other preparation

units.why: "Require your students to cite the specific AI-generated content they use or take ideas from" with in-text and full citations; citation of AI, P24.

units.why: APA instructions say to cite "the company that created the AI and the year"; the citation names tool maker and year, which fits P25 (tool, date details).
units.anchor: put a parenthetical citation with the company that created the AI
units.frag_start: Directly after a sentence or clause

units.why: The reference-list format "Company name. (Year). Title of source [Description]. URL." gives required details of an AI citation; P25.

units.why: MLA guidance: "Do not treat the AI tool as an author", a rule about how to cite AI; closest is P25 (citation detail), partial fit.

units.frag_start: Do not treat the AI tool
units.frag_end: policies developed by various publishers, including the MLA’s journal PMLA.
units.fit_note: A citation-format rule about authorship, not a detail of tool, prompt or date.

units.why: MLA steps say to name the version of the tool as specifically as possible; a tool/version detail of an AI citation, P25.

units.why: MLA step: "Give the date the content was generated"; a date requirement for AI citation, P25.

units.why: Acknowledges "AI usage cannot be fully eliminated for most activities and assessments", a realistic admission that bans cannot be complete; no type directly fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: AI usage cannot be fully eliminated for most activities and assessments
units.uncovered_note: States that AI use cannot be fully eliminated from most activities and assessments, tempering expectations of prevention.

units.why: "Establish clear policies on whether AI tool use is permitted for assignments" leaves permission to each instructor/assignment; P04 (and communicating it).
units.anchor: Establish clear policies on whether AI tool use is permitted for assignments

units.why: Advises assessing the learning process via "lab notebooks, design outlines, or other process documentation"; redesigning grading around process evidence, P35.

units.why: Says faculty can "lean into" AI, "embracing AI technologies and integrating them into their practices"; welcomes AI in teaching, research and administration by faculty, P59.
